items.title: 68239_Ram Ramirez oral history interview
items.q: This little Puerto Rican boy started a riot there in the store; it was through them, and then it spread like wildfire.

ctx.x: That's right. In those days, I mean, the color line was a little funny. That's what made Harlem, I guess, more the color line... Because it made people stick together a little more and get their own thing going, you know. And that's really what happened in Harlem. Harlem just became a community, and this is where the Establishment probably was glad to see it go, because it was becoming... In 1936 it was...or '34... Or was it '36?
